### `lib/src/clock.dart`

- **class `Clock`** — What this package asks of time: what it is now, and something to run later.
  - `DateTime now()` — Now, in UTC, since every instant this package writes down is RFC 3339 UTC (Project Specification §1.4).
  - `JobTimer after(Duration delay, void Function() run)` — Runs [run] once, after [delay].
- **class `JobTimer`** — Something that will run, until it is cancelled.
  - `void cancel()`
- **class `SystemClock`** — Time as the machine keeps it: what a build uses.
  - `const SystemClock()`
- **class `ManualClock`** — A clock a test drives.
  - `ManualClock([DateTime? start])`
  - `void advance(Duration by)` — Moves time on, running every timer that comes due **in the order they come due**, each at its own instant — so a timer set by another timer fires within the same advance when its turn arrives.
  - `int get pending` — How many timers are waiting: a test asserts that nothing was left behind.

### `lib/src/job_record.dart`

- **enum `JobPhase`** — Where a job is, in the seven words a screen may be told (the overview's §4.1).
  - values: `queued`, `working`, `waiting`, `needsAttention`, `done`, `failed`, `cancelled`
  - `bool get isFinished` — Whether nothing more will happen without a person: the phases a scheduler never picks up again.
- **class `JobFailure`** — What went wrong last: a code and the stage it was in.
  - `const JobFailure(this.code, {this.stage})`
  - `final String code` — The code a screen turns into a sentence.
  - `final String? stage` — What the job was doing: `producing`, `ingesting`, `attaching`.
  - `Map<String, Object?> toJson()`
  - `static JobFailure? fromJson(Object? json)`
- **class `JobPayloadRefused`** — A payload this package refuses to keep, and why.
  - `const JobPayloadRefused(this.code, this.path)`
  - `final String code` — `credentialName` — a key called `token`, `secret`, `apiKey`…; `credentialShape` — a value that begins the way a credential does; `address` — an `http` or `https` address; `unwritable` — a value no JSON can hold, or a…
  - `final String path` — Where in the payload it was, dotted: `inputs.0.url`.
- **function** `void checkJobPayload(Map<String, Object?> payload)` — Refuses a payload that holds a credential or an address (§3.1).
- **function** `JobPayloadRefused? jobPayloadProblem(Map<String, Object?> payload)` — What [checkJobPayload] would refuse, or null.
- **class `JobRecord`** — One job, as the journal keeps it.
  - `JobRecord({ required this.id, required this.kind, required this.seq, required this.createdAt, required this.projectKey, this.placeKey, this.phase =…`
  - `static const int schema` — The schema this build writes.
  - `final String id` — Unique on this computer, for as long as the job exists.
  - `final String kind` — What kind of work it is: `upload`, `render`, `text`.
  - `final int seq` — The order it was asked in.
  - `final DateTime createdAt`
  - `final String projectKey` — Which film it belongs to (`filmopen_format`'s `projectKeyOf`).
  - `final String? placeKey` — The place on a page it belongs to, so an element finds its own jobs.
  - `final JobPhase phase`
  - `final String stateCode` — This package's finer word for where the job is — `uploading`, `waitingForConnection`, `heldMetered` — chosen by whoever wrote the runner and turned into a sentence by `filmopen_l10n`.
  - `final Map<String, String> stateArgs` — What the sentence needs: `{'name': 'kira-front.png'}`.
  - `final int attempts` — How many times it has been tried.
  - `final DateTime? notBefore` — The earliest it may be tried again, for a retry that waits.
  - `final JobFailure? lastError`
  - `final Map<String, Object?> payload` — Whoever made the job owns this, and **this package never reads it**.
  - `final Map<String, Object?> unknown` — Keys a build after this one wrote and this one does not know.
  - `JobRecord copyWith({ JobPhase? phase, String? stateCode, Map<String, String>? stateArgs, int? attempts, DateTime? notBefore, bool clearPlaceKey = f…`
  - `Map<String, Object?> toJson()`
  - `static JobRecord? fromJson(Object? json)` — A record read back, or null where the text is not one this build can act on: the caller keeps such a file and does not delete it ([Journal.load]).

### `lib/src/job_view.dart`

- **class `JobAction`** — What may be pressed on a job now.
  - `const JobAction(this.code)`
  - `final String code` — What a widget turns into a label, and what comes back to `act`.
  - `static const JobAction stop` — Stop it; nothing more will be tried.
  - `static const JobAction pause` — Stop it for now, and let it be taken up again.
  - `static const JobAction resume` — Take up a job that was paused or is waiting.
  - `static const JobAction retry` — Try the whole thing again.
  - `static const JobAction attachAgain` — Try only the last stage again: for an insertion, write the reference into the file, at no second upload and no second render.
  - `static const JobAction signIn` — The person has signed in; try again.
  - `static const JobAction dismiss` — Take it off the screen and out of the journal.
  - `static final Set<JobAction> decidedByScheduler` — **The three the scheduler decides by itself**, and `act` asserts that nothing else reaches its last branch, so the set cannot go quietly out of step with the code again (round 2's minor 6).
- **class `JobViewParts`** — What only the job's own kind knows of it: this package never reads a payload, and a runner does.
  - `const JobViewParts({ this.actions = const {}, this.reference, this.previewPath, this.displayName, })`
  - `final Set<JobAction> actions` — What may be pressed on this job, in this phase.
  - `final String? reference` — The media reference it became, so a real tile can wear its badge.
  - `final String? previewPath` — A picture on this computer, where there is one.
  - `final String? displayName`
- **function** `bool sameJobActions(Set<JobAction> a, Set<JobAction> b)` — Two sets of actions that hold the same codes.
- **function** `bool sameStateArgs(Map<String, String> a, Map<String, String> b)` — Two maps of arguments that hold the same pairs.
- **class `JobView`** — One job, as a screen is given it.
  - `const JobView({ required this.id, required this.kind, required this.phase, this.stateCode = '', this.stateArgs = const {}, this.progress, this.acti…`
  - `final String id`
  - `final String kind` — `upload` · `render` · `text` … — it picks an icon, and nothing else.
  - `final JobPhase phase`
  - `final String stateCode` — The package's own finer word: `uploading`, `waitingForConnection`, `heldMetered` ….
  - `final Map<String, String> stateArgs`
  - `final double? progress` — Null draws an indeterminate mark; a number only where something measured it.
  - `final Set<JobAction> actions`
  - `final String? placeKey` — The place it belongs to, so an element finds its own.
  - `final String? reference`
  - `final String? previewPath`
  - `final String? displayName`

- **class `JournalFiles`** — The bytes a journal is kept in, behind an interface so that the rules above are one implementation and the platform is another: a folder on disk ([journalFilesIn]), or a map in memory ([MemoryJournalFiles]) for tests,…
  - `Future<List<String>> list()` — Every file in the folder, by name.
  - `Future<void> sweepTemporary()` — Clears whatever a build killed mid-write left behind, where the platform has such leavings at all.

  - `Future<void> write(String name, String text)` — Writes one file whole, replacing what was there.
  - `Future<void> remove(String name)` — Removes one file; does nothing where there is none.
- **class `MemoryJournalFiles`** — A journal in memory: the web, a test, and a film that has no folder, whose jobs are of this session alone (5-2c's D8).
  - `final Map<String, String> files` — What is there, by name.
- **class `UnknownJournalFile`** — A journal file this build will not read, kept where it is.
  - `const UnknownJournalFile(this.name, {required this.reason, this.schema})`
  - `final String name`
  - `final String reason` — **Why it was not read**, since the two cases want different words (round 2's B7): `schema` — a build after this one wrote it, and this one must leave it alone — or `unreadable` — it declares this build's own schema an…
  - `final int? schema` — The schema it declares, where it declares one a reader can see.
- **class `JournalLoad`** — What one read of the journal found.
  - `const JournalLoad(this.records, this.unknown)`
  - `final List<JobRecord> records` — The jobs, in the order they were asked for ([JobRecord.seq]).
  - `final List<UnknownJournalFile> unknown` — Files kept and not read — **the first time this journal meets each, and not again**, so a film opened and closed all afternoon does not say the same thing every time.
- **class `BadJobIdException`** — An id that cannot be a file name.
  - `const BadJobIdException(this.id)`
  - `final String id`
- **class `Journal`** — The jobs kept on this computer.
  - `Future<JournalLoad> load()`
  - `Future<void> put(JobRecord record)` — Writes one job, whole.
  - `Future<void> remove(String id)`
- **class `FileJournal`** — The one implementation of the journal's rules, over whatever [JournalFiles] it is given.
  - `FileJournal(this.files)`
  - `final JournalFiles files`
  - `static const String extension` — What a job's file is called.
  - `static String fileNameFor(String id)`
- **class `MemoryJournal`** — A journal that lives for this run of the application: the web, a test, and every job of a film that has no folder (5-2c's D8).
  - `MemoryJournal([MemoryJournalFiles? files])`

### `lib/src/lease.dart`

- **class `JobLease`** — The lease over one journal folder.
  - `JobLease(this.files, { required this.clock, required this.token, this.stale = const Duration(seconds: 30), })`
  - `static const String fileName` — The file the lease is kept in.
  - `final JournalFiles files`
  - `final Clock clock`
  - `final String token` — This holder's own token: unique to this run of this build.
  - `final Duration stale` — How long a lease stands without being renewed.
  - `bool get held` — Whether this holder may work jobs.
  - `Future<bool> acquire()` — Takes the lease if it is free, stale, or already this holder's.
  - `Future<bool> renew()` — Keeps the lease.
  - `void startRenewing()` — **Keeps the lease by itself, until [stopRenewing]** (round 6's finding 3).
  - `void Function()? onLost` — **Told when a renewal finds the lease gone**, so that whoever holds work in flight can stop it (§9.4's review, finding 3).
  - `void stopRenewing()` — Stops [startRenewing]'s timer.
  - `bool get renewingForTest` — Whether [startRenewing]'s chain is still going, for a test that asks whether it stopped.
  - `Future<void> release()` — Gives the lease up, so that another build takes it at once rather than after [stale].

- **class `ProducerContext`** — What a producer is given when it starts: the clock, and nothing else.

  - `ProducerRun start(Map<String, Object?> request, ProducerContext context)` — Begins.
  - `ProducerRun? restore(Map<String, Object?> saved, ProducerContext context)` — Takes up a run this build left behind, from what [ProducerRun.toJson] wrote.
- **class `ProducerRun`** — One run of a producer.
  - `Stream<ProducerEvent> get events` — A state and its progress, then [Produced] or [ProducerFailed].
  - `Future<void> cancel()` — Asks it to stop.
  - `Map<String, Object?> toJson()` — What [Producer.restore] would be given.
  - `Future<void> acknowledge()` — Said once the items are safe — written into the store and recorded.
- **class `ProducerEvent`** — What a run says as it goes.

### `lib/src/scheduler.dart`

- **class `JobControl`** — **A lane is work that shares a limit**, named by a string and given a capacity through [JobScheduler.setCapacity].
  - `bool get cancelled` — Whether a stop or a pause has been asked for.
  - `void report({String? stateCode, Map<String, String>? stateArgs, double? progress})` — Says where the job has got to.
  - `Future<bool> remember(Map<String, Object?> values)` — **Writes something into the job's own payload, now**, so that a later attempt — after a retry, after a restart — reads what this one decided.
- **class `JobRunner`** — How one kind of job is done.
  - `String get kind` — The `kind` of the records this runs.
  - `String laneOf(JobRecord record)` — Which lane this job's work shares a limit with.
  - `JobViewParts partsOf(JobRecord record)` — What only this kind knows of the job, for the view a screen is given.
  - `Future<JobOutcome> run(JobRecord record, JobControl control)` — Does the work.
- **class `JobOutcome`** — What a run of a job came to.
  - `const JobOutcome()`
- **class `JobDone`** — It happened, and what it was for is true.
  - `const JobDone({this.stateCode = ''})`
  - `final String stateCode`
- **class `JobFailed`** — It did not happen, and nothing more will be tried.
  - `const JobFailed(this.code, {this.stage})`
  - `final String code`
  - `final String? stage`
- **class `JobRetryLater`** — It did not happen, and asking again later might work.
  - `const JobRetryLater(this.code, {this.stage, required this.after})`
  - `final String code`
  - `final String? stage`
  - `final Duration after` — How long to wait.
- **class `JobWaiting`** — It stopped, and will go on by itself when something changes — the connection, the film being opened again.
  - `const JobWaiting(this.code, {this.args = const {}})`
  - `final String code`
  - `final Map<String, String> args`
- **class `JobNeedsAttention`** — It stopped, and nothing will move until a person presses one of the job's actions.
  - `const JobNeedsAttention(this.code, {this.stage, this.args = const {}})`
  - `final String code`
  - `final String? stage`
  - `final Map<String, String> args`
- **class `JobCancelled`** — It stopped because a person asked.
  - `const JobCancelled()`
- **class `JobScheduler`** — The jobs of this computer, run in order and within their lanes.
  - `JobScheduler({ required Journal journal, required Clock clock, JobLease? lease, this.defaultCapacity`
  - `final int defaultCapacity` — What a lane holds when nobody has said.
  - `Stream<List<JobView>> get changes` — What every screen watches.
  - `List<JobView> get views` — Every job, in the order they were asked for.
  - `List<JobView> viewsFor(String placeKey)` — The jobs of one place, in the order they were asked for.
  - `void register(JobRunner runner)` — Registers how a kind of job is done.
  - `void setCapacity(String lane, int capacity)` — How many of a lane's jobs may run at once.
  - `int capacityOf(String lane)`
  - `void holdLane(String lane, String code, {Set<JobAction> lifted = const {}, Map<String, String> args = const {}})` — Holds a whole lane, with the code that says why, **what lifts it**, and what its sentence needs.
  - `void releaseLane(String lane, String code)` — Lets go of **one reason** [lane] is held for, and, where it was the last, takes up every job **a hold paused**.
  - `String? holdOn(String lane)` — The code a lane is held by — the first reason that remains, which is the one a screen is shown — or null where it is free.
  - `void theLeaseIsGone()` — **The lease is gone: stop the bytes that are already moving** (§9.4's review, finding 3).
  - `List<String> holdsOn(String lane)` — Every reason [lane] is held for, oldest first.
  - `Future<void> restore({String? projectKey})` — Reads the journal and takes up what is there.
  - `Future<List<UnknownJournalFile>> unreadable()` — Files that a load would not read, for the caller to log once.
  - `Future<JobRecord> submit({ required String kind, required String projectKey, String? placeKey, Map<String, Object?> payload = const {}, })` — Asks for a job.
  - `Future<void> act(String id, JobAction action)` — **The control road.** Answered at once, whatever the lanes are doing: it takes no slot, waits on no capacity and joins no queue, so a person can stop a job while every lane is full.
  - `Future<void> wake(bool Function(JobRecord record) which)` — Takes up every waiting job [which] names: the film was opened, the connection came back, the person signed in.
  - `Future<void> whenIdle()` — **Answers when nothing is running**, so that a window closing can give a copy in flight its bounded time (milestone 5-2d §3.5, as the open drafts have theirs).
  - `Future<void> forgetOldDone(Duration after)` — **Forgets the jobs that are done and old** (the plan's §6: a *done* job leaves the journal when its element has shown it once, or after a day; one needing attention stays until the person dismisses it).
  - `Future<void> dispose()` — Stops taking up work and leaves no timer behind.
